description.narrative: Driving private sector (together with civil society, Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and Governments) towards being sustainable and inclusive. This is achieved by empowering and supporting enterprises to embrace sustainability in their business models, reduce their carbon footprint and negative impact on the planet, and increase their positive impact on people while generating profit.
Private sector, government, civil society and academia

a. Increase awareness, knowledge and social dialogue on the importance and opportunities of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), sustainability and inclusiveness among Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and corporate. b. Expand and strengthen the application of sustainable inclusive business principles, strategies and practices within businesses and organisations (small, medium and large).

title.narrative: Enhancing staff capacity through continuous training and staff development.

comment.narrative: 4 team building sessions were executed aligning to the institutional strategy that has a focus on building the capacity of its personnel.

title.narrative: Number of policy interventions/input submitted to/through KEPSA sector boards.

comment.narrative: SIB-K actively collaborated with the Ministry of Environment and Forestry to support the development of the National Sustainable Waste Management Act of 2022, the Environmental Management and Coordination (Extended Producer Responsibility) Regulations review. Furthermore, the team contributed significantly to developing the No Single-Use Plastic Ban action plan for protected areas in close collaboration with the Environmental Sector Board. In addition to their involvement in policy review, SIB-K also played a key role in drafting the Green Public Procurement Framework. Furthermore, SIB-K was part of the technical working group that supported the Ministry in developing an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) guideline, highlighting their expertise in this area. It is worth noting that developing regulations or policies requires meticulous technical and legal reviews, which SIB-K diligently participated in.

The success of the first year's efforts in submitting proposals was evident in the increased number of training sessions and consultancies achieved in the second year. A total of 17 training sessions were conducted, surpassing the target of 16.

title.narrative: # of organisations adopting SIB practices or changing their operations to become more sustainable and inclusive

comment.narrative: a notable accomplishment was seen in the adoption of sustainable business practices by 60 organisations, against a target of 90. This can be reflected with the increase in the target after an overachievement in the first year.

14 consultancies were implemented, slightly below the target of 17. There was a decline in the number of consultancies in the third year as the focus shifted toward executing the awarded projects. This highlights the strategic shift towards project implementation and demonstrates the overall progress made toward promoting sustainable and inclusive business practices in the target organisations.

During the project's second year, a noteworthy achievement was the successful training of additional staff members, resulting in a total of 14 staff being trained. These trained staff had the opportunity to attend conferences and share their research findings, leading to the development of policy recommendations. The international conferences provided valuable learning experiences for the staff as they were able to interact and learn from professionals in other countries, enriching their knowledge and expertise. In the third year, the organisation conducted two team-building sessions, which facilitated cross-learning among staff and helped shape the organisational culture in alignment with the new organisational strategy.

In the first year, 41 businesses were engaged, but this number increased significantly in the second year, with 82 businesses engaged, marking the highest engagement level during the project period. The second year also saw the onboarding of more projects, which contributed to the sourcing of resources to sustain the project in its third year of implementation. A total of 134 businesses were engaged against a target of 59 companies.
Overall, the organisation achieved training 14 staff members, conducting 12 training sessions, and organising 4 team building sessions.

comment.narrative: SIB-K participated in 341 sessions, with the most meetings and forums conducted in the second and final year, totaling 142 and 147, respectively.

title.narrative: # of companies, academia, civil society and government agencies participating in the engagement.

comment.narrative: The introduction of a virtual platform allowed for both in-person and virtual attendance, further expanding the reach of the conferences. In total, 1,250 companies, academia, civil society, governmental organisations, and individuals attended the annual conference, surpassing the target of 750 attendees.
SIB-K participated in 46 sessions, including panel discussions and events, which came close to achieving the target of 50 sessions.

The project surpassed the target on impressions on Twitter, LinkedIn, Facebook. The improvement can be attributed to the project’s communication strategy to use online platforms as the major communication channels during the COVID-19 pandemic. The target has been revised upwards from 1,500,000 impressions to 2,400,000. The project achieve 2,964,922 impressions.

title.narrative: # of companies reached via the portal

description.narrative: Ensure website has current and accurate sustainable inclusive business information and is interactive.

comment.narrative: The website was refurbished in 2019, an increase in reach has been experienced this year due to review and updating of content that is relevant to businesses and aligned to the thematic areas. The portal played a crucial role in disseminating knowledge, as evidenced by website analytics showing a reach 70,494 visits were achieved during the project period.

title.narrative: Maintaining a sustainable inclusive business database.

description.narrative: Updating, cleaning and verifying data on businesses.

comment.narrative: SIB-K increased its outreach and raised awareness about regulations, policies, and best practices related to sustainability. The contacts within the database formed a community where information could be shared and linkages could be facilitated. Despite the project ultimately achieving 1523 businesses in the database, the first year saw a significant acquisition of business contacts.

title.narrative: # of successful partnerships made between businesses/organisations.

comment.narrative: 22 business partnerships were established during the project period. The annual conferences presented the best opportunity to facilitate and broker partnerships.
